title: curated severity/progression literature pass (PMC-OA dominant-sequela join) — S/P lift / new order-lock

litcurate_join.exact_sentence: Conclusions NPD type A is a rare and fatal disorder that starts in early infancy and progressively worsens, leading to the patient’s death by two to three years of age.
Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a rare, progressive neuromuscular disorder primarily affecting boys, and it follows a predictable course.

litcurate_excluded.considered_statement: The severe phenotype is known as Hurler syndrome (MPS IH; OMIM 607014 ), and other forms are classified as attenuated MPS I (Hurler-Scheie syndrome, MPS IH-S, OMIM 607015 ; Scheie syndrome, MPS IS, OMIM 607016 ).
litcurate_excluded.exclusion_reason: the 'severe' descriptor here distinguishes Hurler from the ATTENUATED MPS I forms (Hurler-Scheie, Scheie) -- comparative nosological framing that names where Hurler sits on the MPS I continuum, not an anchored disease-level severity for Hurler's dominant untreated sequela; per the BURDEN_INDEX rule, comparative references to other forms do not anchor an entity's own severity. S not lifted

litcurate_excluded.considered_statement: Clinically, the manifestations of Hurler syndrome may vary widely, presenting a spectrum from mild to severe.
litcurate_excluded.exclusion_reason: a second OA source explicitly predicates WITHIN-ENTITY variability of Hurler syndrome ('may vary widely, presenting a spectrum from mild to severe'); under the BURDEN_INDEX severity-spectrum rule a mild-to-severe range is scored at the [H] midpoint, not at an extreme, so a clean non-spectrum disease-level severe tier is not defensibly isolable for Hurler. S kept at the [H] spectrum midpoint

litcurate_excluded.considered_statement: Clinical phenotypes of PD range from the severe infantile-onset form (IOPD), characterised clinically by cardiomyopathy and hypotonia within the first days to weeks of life, to the late-onset form (LOPD), which involves a more slowly progressive myopathy.
litcurate_excluded.exclusion_reason: the cohort entity is the UMBRELLA Pompe disease / GSD II, and the cited sentence states its progression as an explicit RANGE -- 'from the severe infantile-onset form (IOPD) ... to the late-onset form (LOPD), which involves a more slowly progressive myopathy' (rapid/severe infantile pole to slowly-progressive late-onset pole); a single disease-level progression tier is not defensible for an umbrella that spans both poles. P stays at the [H] spectrum midpoint (0.5), which correctly represents the umbrella

litcurate_excluded.considered_statement: Discussion Initially described by Menke in 1954 as a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease, the cause of MSUD was described as a deficiency of the BCKAD complex, which functions to break the amino acids leucine, isoleucine, and valine [ 3 ].
litcurate_excluded.exclusion_reason: the only OA 'rapidly progressive neurodegenerative' phrasing is an explicitly HISTORICAL characterization ('Initially described by Menke in 1954 as ...'), reporting the 1954 description of the classic untreated form rather than a current disease-level magnitude; and the cohort entity spans classic / intermediate / intermittent / thiamine-responsive variant forms (a severity/progression spectrum). P left [O], not lifted

litcurate_excluded.considered_statement: Because of lack of screening and insidious onset of the chronic form of HT1, there was a diagnosis delay around five months after the onset of symptoms.
litcurate_excluded.exclusion_reason: the available OA progression statement is specific to the CHRONIC form of HT1 ('insidious onset of the chronic form') and concerns diagnostic delay, not a disease-level untreated-progression magnitude; hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 presents in distinct acute (rapidly progressive, infantile) and chronic (insidious) forms -- a form-dependent spectrum -- and the other OA statements describe NTBC-treated cohorts. P left [O], not lifted
